QF.id: Analysis of Equity and Debt Instruments_4

question.text: Which of the following is NOT excluded from the definition of "capital asset" under the Income Tax Act?

answer.text: Personal effects such as wearing apparel and furniture

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pages 175-176, the definition of capital asset excludes stock-in-trade, personal effects, and rural agricultural land in India. However, jewellery and listed art/collection assets are specifically NOT treated as personal effects, even if meant for personal use, and therefore remain capital assets. The Trap: Candidates may assume that any item used personally falls within the personal-effects exclusion. The source explicitly carves jewellery out of the personal-effects exclusion, so jewellery continues to be a capital asset. Note: Apply the page 175-176 exclusion list together with its carve-out for jewellery, archaeological collections, drawings, paintings, sculptures, and any work of art.
